records.text: Elisoub the high priest and his brothers the priests arose and built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and consecrated as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Ananeel,
and alongside the sons of the men of Jericho, and alongside the sons of Zakchour son of Amari.
The sons of Asana built the Fish Gate. They roofed it and set up its doors, locks and bars.
Next to them, from Ramoth, a son of Ouria son of Akos took charge. Next to them Mosollam son of Barachias son of Masezebel took charge. Next to them Sadok son of Baana took charge.
Next to them the Thekoin took charge, but the adoreem did not bring their necks into their service.
Ioida son of Phasek and Mesoulam son of Basodia repaired the gate of Isana. They roofed it and set up its doors, locks and bars.
Next to them Ananias son of Rokeim repaired, and they left Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them Raphaia, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
Next to them Iedaia son of Eromaph repaired, opposite his house. Next to him Atous son of Asbania repaired.
As second, Melchias son of Eram and Asoub son of Phaathmoab repaired, as far as the Tower of the Thannourim.
Anoun and the inhabitants of Zano repaired the Valley Gate. They built it and set up its doors, locks and bars, and a thousand cubits of wall as far as the Dung Gate.
Melchia son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Bethacharm, repaired the Dung Gate, he and his sons. They covered it and set up its doors, locks and bars,
After him Benjamin and Asoub repaired opposite their house. After him Azaria son of Maasea son of Anania repaired beside his house.
After him Bani son of Enadad repaired a second section, from Bethazaria to the corner and to the bend
The Nathinim were living on the Ophal, as far as the garden of the Water Gate toward the east, and the projecting tower.
After him the Thekoin repaired a second section opposite the great projecting tower, as far as the wall of the Ophla.
After him Saddouk son of Emmer repaired opposite his house. After him Samaia son of Sechenia, keeper of the East Gate, repaired.
After him Anania son of Selemia and Anoum, the sixth son of Seleph, repaired a second section. After him Mesoulam son of Barchia repaired opposite his treasury chamber.
Then the whole congregation of the sons of Israel departed from Moses’ presence.
Everyone whose heart prompted him and whose soul was willing brought an offering to the Lord for all the work of the Tent of Testimony, for all its service, and for all the holy robes.
The men brought from the women, everyone whose heart approved: seals, earrings, rings, chains, bracelets, and every gold object—all who brought gold offerings to the Lord.
Everyone who had fine linen, skins dyed blue, or rams’ skins dyed red brought them.
Everyone contributing silver or bronze brought offerings to the Lord, and those who had decay-resistant wood for all the work of preparation brought it.
The leaders brought the emerald stones and the stones for setting in the shoulder-piece and the oracle-piece,
and the compounds, the anointing oil, and the compounded incense.
Every man and woman whose mind inclined them to come and do all the work the Lord had commanded through Moses—the sons of Israel brought an offering to the Lord.
The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah in King Zedekiah’s tenth year, which was the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
Zedekiah will certainly not be saved from the Chaldeans’ hand, but will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king. His mouth will speak to his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes.
Zedekiah will enter Babylon and remain there.
A great outcry arose from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.
Some said, “With our sons and daughters we are many. We must obtain grain, eat, and live.”
Others said, “Our fields, our vineyards and our houses—we are pledging them. We must obtain grain and eat.”

Now our flesh is like our brothers’ flesh, and our sons like their sons. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are being subjected. There is no power in our hands, and our fields and vineyards belong to the honored men.”
I was deeply grieved when I heard their outcry and these words.
My heart took counsel within me. I contended with the honored men and leaders and said to them, “You are making demands, each against his brother!” I brought a great assembly against them,
and said to them, “We have bought our Jewish brothers who were being sold to the nations, of our own free will. And are you selling your brothers?” They fell quiet and found no answer.
I said, “What you are doing is not good. Not so! In the fear of our God you shall depart from the reproach of the nations, our enemies.
My brothers, my acquaintances and I have also put silver and grain at their disposal. Let us, I pray, relinquish this exaction.
Please restore to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive trees and houses; and from the silver, bring out for them the grain, wine and oil.”
They said, “We will return it and ask nothing from them. We will do as you say.” I called the priests and made them swear to act according to this word.

I shook out my wrap and said, “So may God shake out from his house and his labor every man who does not uphold this word. So shall he be shaken out and empty.” All the assembly said, “Amen,” and praised the Lord. The people carried out this word.

From the day he appointed me to be their ruler in the land of Judah—from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Arthasastha, twelve years—I and my brothers did not eat their coerced provision,

and as for the former exactions, which before me they laid heavily upon them: they took from them bread and wine, and, at the last, silver—forty didrachms. Their shaken-out men exercise authority over the people, but I did not act that way, because of the fear of God.
At my table were the Jews, one hundred and fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations around us.

Each day one young bull, six choice sheep and a he-goat were prepared for me. Every ten days there was wine in abundance for everyone. Along with these things, I did not demand bread from coercion, because the service weighed heavily on this people.
Remember me for good, God, for everything I have done for this people.
Joachas was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Amital daughter of Jeremiah, from Lemna.
He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Nechao removed him at Deblatha in Emath’s land so that he would not reign in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.
Pharaoh Nechao made Eliakim, son of Josiah king of Judah, king over them in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Joakim. He took Joachas and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.
Samuel said to every man of Israel, “Behold, I have listened to your voice in everything you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
Now the king walks before you. I have grown old and will sit down, and my sons are here among you. I have walked before you from my youth to this day.
When the wall had been built, I set up the doors, and the gatekeepers, singers and Levites were appointed.

and I said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until the sun is up. While they are still keeping watch, let the doors be closed and wedged fast. Appoint advance guards from those living in Jerusalem, each at his guard post and each opposite his house.”
The city was broad and large, but the people in it were few, and no houses had been built.
After the next day Moses sat to judge the people, and all the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.
And when Jethro saw all that he did to the people, he said, “What is this that you do to the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?”
Moses said to his father-in-law, “The people come to me to seek judgment from God.
When they have a dispute and come to me, I judge each case and instruct them in God’s ordinances and His law.”
And Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “You are not doing this rightly.
You shall be worn out with unbearable exhaustion, both you and all this people who are with you; this matter is heavy for you, and you cannot do it alone.
Now therefore listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God shall be with you. Represent the people in matters pertaining to God, and bring their words to God.
And you shall solemnly instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law, and show them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do.
If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to stand; and all this people shall come to their own place in peace.”
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times. They brought every weighty matter to Moses, but judged every light matter themselves.
Thus said the Lord: They will again say this word in Judah’s land and its cities when I return its captivity: Blessed is the Lord over the righteous mountain, His holy mountain,
and those dwelling in Judah’s cities and all its land together with a farmer; and he will be lifted up with a flock.
Because I filled every thirsty soul to abundance and filled every hungry soul.
Therefore I awoke and saw, and my sleep became sweet to me.
Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will sow Israel and Judah with human seed and livestock seed.
And just as I watched over them to tear down and harm, so I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.
